objectives.description: Comprehension: ability to read and understand standard written documents in French; two passages each of about 150 words with short questions.

Structure: parts of speech (grammatical categories); articles — definite, indefinite, partitive (gender and number); verbs — types (regular and irregular), common moods and tenses, standard expressions (avoir + noun, venir de + infinitive); nouns — complements, gender, number; pronouns — personal, possessive, indefinite, demonstrative, relative, impersonal; adjectives — possessive, demonstrative, indefinite, interrogative (agreement and position); adverbs — formation and position, special adverbs; negatives — negative expressions (ne…pas, ne…rien, ne…jamais, etc.); conjunctions in common use; prepositions; sentence patterns; voice — active/passive; direct speech/reported speech; compound and complex sentences; idiomatic expressions and proverbs; forms of writing (formal/informal); common figures of speech (similes, metaphors, hyperboles); structures of major actes de parole.
Essay: ability to write freely and correctly on topics of general interest using appropriate structures, registers and tenses (approximately 100 words).
Letter writing: ability to write formal and informal letters in French using appropriate format and register.

subStrands.name: Listening Comprehension, Reading Aloud and Conversation

objectives.description: Listening comprehension: ability to listen to and understand a straightforward passage in French (about 200 words); answer 10 questions based on the passage read aloud by the examiner.
Reading: ability to read aloud a simple passage (about 100 words) with appropriate pronunciation and fluency.

Conversation: ability to express oneself freely in a dialogue (responding to a minimum of ten questions) and exposition (making a minimum of 5 sentences on a given topic); topics drawn from general and contemporary interests such as sports, health, leisure, education, politics, culture, etc.
